newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-There are important changes in the pipeline for pensions, with the pensioning off age to settle at 65 for men and 60 for women. Other changes involve lump sum payments and conditions for receipt of pension: all the measures will be valid as of January 1, 1998.

--Tariff increases by public enterprises and organisations (DEKOs) will not be more than inflation, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said, a day after the announcement that public transport fares would be increased by 33 percent.

--Conservative opposition New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis stressed the need to cut back on state spending, reduce fiscal deficits and for a bold privatisation programme in his meeting with the leadership of the Federation of Greek Industries yesterday.
--The Greek government must take additional measures if it is to achieve convergence with the countries of the other EU member-states, the European Commission said in its report, presented yesterday.

--The tariff increases in DEKOs later this year will be the first increase in a sixteen months. Increases are expected to be below the rate of inflation set as a target for the end of the year - 4.5 percent.
--Papandoniou has told US and Greek-American investors that Greece can act as a base for the efforts to reorganise the southern Balkans and the Black Sea countries.

--Greece telecoms organisation OTE's second share float is expected on the market by June although there are concerns about the effect of France Telecom's presence at the same time on international money markets.

--Greece and Italy are the only countries not to meet Maastrict criteria for inclusion in Economic and Monetary Union in 1999, according to the European Commission report on member-states' economic developments in 1997 and 1998.

--OTE's board yesterday approved the payment of a 180 drachma per share dividend, or 76 billion drachmas in total. OTE has posted gross profits of 250.,2 billion drachmas with net profits of 152.2 billion drachmas.
--Commercial Bank has posted a profit of 12.06 billion drachmas in 1996 and a dividend of 300 drachmas for shareholders.
--A new committee is to be established to control and monitor food destined for consumers. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
